title: Offshore salt and moisture accumulation design sensitivity (not experimentally determined maximum corrosion rates)
basis: User-requested increased chloride/wetting exposure screening on the external, non-H2S pig-magazine; not a verified material-specific maximum or design allowance.

reference_standards.application: C5 and CX first-year rate ranges apply to standard carbon-steel reference specimens, not exact magazine metal loss, not specific to AISI 1020 normalized, and not transferable to Al 6061/7075 or austenitic stainless steels.
High-durability offshore protective paint systems for carbon-steel structures; not corrosion rate acceleration multiplier.
An example cyclic salt/wetting method; it does not provide a universal material-specific multiplier or convert test duration to offshore service life.

upper_envelope_disclaimer: No reviewed chloride paper measured exactly 2x, 3x, or 5x service rate for all five candidates. These are transparent multipliers for design sensitivity only, NOT worst-case physical bounds or standard-defined protection factors. Actual localized pitting can be deeper even if uniform loss is small.
spatial_disclaimer: The geometry attention index is an illustrative surface-orientation/elevation proxy; it has not been calibrated to salt deposition, wetting hours, seawater pooling, chloride concentration, coating state, or pit kinetics. Magazine motion changes orientation.
wall_disclaimer: Any computed wall number is a one-face hypothetical uniform-equivalent recession from a 10 mm nominal chamber tube, not actual shell thinning, structural integrity, pressure rating, service life, or a paired inner-outer assessment.
scenario_use: Option to test influence of arbitrary higher-than-benchmark uniform-equivalent rates on color and numerical indicators before obtaining site-specific cyclic corrosion or outdoor exposure measurements.
priority_tests: Measure airborne salt deposition and time of wetness at the actual offshore installation.
Verify drainage and sealed chamber water exposure while the drum indexes and parks.
Run identical marine cyclic wet/dry tests on five exact grades and selected coatings, with pit depth and mass loss.
Use worst measured penetration (not arbitrary multiplier) for updated material-selection / wall assessment.
